events.text: Spanish and imperial forces destroyed the main Swedish army in southern Germany.

events.name: Peace of Prague
events.text: Saxony and most Protestant princes made peace with the emperor.

steps.title: France enters
steps.text: Cardinal Richelieu brought Catholic France into the war against the Habsburgs in 1635 to break their encirclement of France. Sweden recovered under Baner with a victory at Wittstock, Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar took Breisach and cut the Spanish Road, and in 1643 the young Duke of Enghien broke the famous Spanish tercios at Rocroi.

events.name: Battle of Wittstock
events.text: Baner's Swedes defeated the imperial and Saxon army in Brandenburg.

events.name: Siege of Breisach
events.text: The fall of the Rhine fortress cut Spain's land route from Italy to the Netherlands.

events.name: Battle of Rocroi
events.text: The French broke the Spanish infantry, ending its reputation for invincibility.

steps.title: Peace of Westphalia
steps.text: Torstensson's Swedes destroyed an imperial army at Jankau and advanced toward Vienna, while Turenne and Wrangel ravaged Bavaria. After years of talks at Munster and Osnabruck, the Peace of Westphalia ended the war in October 1648, leaving Germany devastated and France and Sweden the winners.

events.name: Battle of Jankau
events.text: Torstensson's Swedes destroyed the emperor's last major army in Bohemia.

events.name: Battle of Zusmarshausen
events.text: French and Swedish troops defeated the last imperial and Bavarian field army.

events.name: Peace of Westphalia
events.text: Treaties at Munster and Osnabruck gave Sweden and France new lands and the German princes sovereignty.

name: Qing (Manchu) invasions of Korea
summary: The Manchus of the Later Jin, at war with Ming China, twice invaded Joseon Korea to end its loyalty to the Ming. The first invasion in 1627 forced a 'brotherly' alliance; the second in 1636 to 1637, led by Hong Taiji as emperor of the new Qing dynasty, trapped King Injo in Namhansanseong and forced him to kneel in surrender. Korea became a Qing tributary, cut its ties to the Ming and turned inward for two centuries.

steps.label: Jan to Mar 1627
steps.title: First invasion
steps.text: Hong Taiji, the new Later Jin khan, sent his cousin Amin across the frozen Yalu with about 30,000 men to punish Korea for helping the Ming. The Manchus stormed Uiju and Anju and occupied Pyongyang, and King Injo fled from Seoul to Ganghwa Island. Short of supplies, the Jin agreed to a treaty making Korea its 'younger brother' and withdrew.

fronts.label: Limit of the Jin advance, Mar 1627

events.name: Fall of Uiju
events.text: The border fortress fell on the first day of the invasion.

events.name: Battle of Anju
events.text: The Manchus stormed Anju and its commander blew himself up rather than surrender.

events.name: Peace at Ganghwa
events.text: Korea accepted a 'brotherly' relationship with the Later Jin but did not break with the Ming.

steps.title: The Qing demand submission
steps.text: Korea kept supporting the Ming while the Manchus grew stronger: in 1629 Hong Taiji raided through the Great Wall to the gates of Beijing, and by 1635 the Mongols of Inner Mongolia had submitted. In 1636 at Mukden he proclaimed the Qing dynasty with himself as emperor and demanded that Korea acknowledge him as its overlord. King Injo's court refused.

events.name: Raid on Beijing
events.text: Hong Taiji's army ravaged the Beijing region before withdrawing with plunder.

events.name: Proclamation of the Qing
events.text: Hong Taiji declared himself emperor of the Great Qing; the Korean envoys refused to bow.

steps.label: Dec 1636 to Jan 1637
steps.title: Second invasion and Namhansanseong
steps.text: In December 1636 Hong Taiji crossed the frozen Yalu with about 120,000 men. A cavalry vanguard ignored General Im Gyeong-eop's fortress at Baengma and raced to Seoul in under two weeks, cutting off the road to Ganghwa. The royal family escaped to the island, but King Injo had to take refuge in the mountain fortress of Namhansanseong, where the Qing besieged him.

events.name: Baengma fortress
events.text: Im Gyeong-eop held his fortress, but the Qing simply rode past it.

events.name: Siege of Namhansanseong
events.text: Some 13,000 defenders with little food were surrounded in deep winter.

steps.label: Jan to Feb 1637
steps.title: Surrender at Samjeondo
steps.text: Provincial relief armies marching to the king were beaten one by one, and Dorgon crossed to Ganghwa and captured the royal family. With food running out, King Injo came down from the fortress and kowtowed to Hong Taiji at Samjeondo on the Han River. Korea became a Qing tributary, broke with the Ming and sent two princes to Mukden as hostages.

events.name: Battle of Ssangnyeong
events.text: A large Korean relief army from Gyeongsang was routed by a small Qing cavalry force.

events.name: Fall of Ganghwa
events.text: Dorgon's troops crossed by boat and captured the queen and princes.

events.name: Surrender at Samjeondo
events.text: Injo bowed nine times to Hong Taiji and accepted Qing overlordship.

name: English Civil War
summary: A struggle over power, taxes and religion between Charles I and Parliament became a civil war across England, Scotland and Ireland. Parliament, allied with the Scottish Covenanters and later fighting with its own New Model Army under Fairfax and Cromwell, won the first war, then beat the King's Scottish allies, executed Charles in 1649 and conquered Ireland and Scotland. Britain briefly became a republic, and the war established that a king could not rule without Parliament.

steps.title: War begins: Edgehill
steps.text: After years of quarrels over taxes, religion and control of the army, Charles I raised his standard at Nottingham in August 1642. Parliament held London, the navy and the rich southeast; the King drew support from the north, west and Wales. The first battle at Edgehill was a draw, and the King's advance on London stopped at Turnham Green, so he made Oxford his capital.

events.name: King raises his standard
events.text: Charles declared war on Parliament at Nottingham Castle.

events.name: Battle of Edgehill
events.text: The first battle of the war ended indecisively.

events.name: Turnham Green
events.text: London's trained bands faced down the King, who fell back to Oxford.

steps.title: The Scots join: Marston Moor
steps.text: The Royalists did well in 1643, so Parliament allied with the Scottish Covenanters in the Solemn League and Covenant. In 1644 Leven's Scots marched south and besieged York with Parliament's northern armies. Prince Rupert rode to the rescue, but at Marston Moor Cromwell's cavalry and the allied foot destroyed his army and the north was lost to the King, though Charles trapped and captured Essex's infantry at Lostwithiel in Cornwall.

events.name: Solemn League and Covenant
events.text: The Scots agreed to send an army to fight for Parliament.

events.name: Battle of Marston Moor
events.text: The largest battle of the war cost the King the north of England.

events.name: Battle of Lostwithiel
events.text: Essex's infantry surrendered to the King in Cornwall.

steps.title: New Model Army: Naseby
steps.text: Parliament created the professional New Model Army under Sir Thomas Fairfax with Oliver Cromwell commanding the horse. At Naseby in June 1645 it destroyed the King's main field army, and the Royalist strongholds fell one by one. In Scotland Montrose won a string of victories for the King until David Leslie beat him at Philiphaugh, and in May 1646 Charles surrendered to the Scots.

events.name: Battle of Naseby
events.text: The New Model Army destroyed the King's infantry and captured his papers.

events.name: Battle of Philiphaugh
events.text: David Leslie surprised and routed Montrose's army.

events.name: King surrenders to the Scots
events.text: Charles gave himself up to the Scottish army near Newark, ending the first civil war.

steps.title: Second Civil War and the King's execution
steps.text: Charles plotted with a faction of Scots, the Engagers, who invaded England for him in 1648 while Royalists rose in Kent, Essex and Wales. Cromwell crushed the Scots at Preston and Fairfax starved out Colchester. Convinced the King could not be trusted, the army purged Parliament, and Charles I was tried and beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall in January 1649.

events.name: Siege of Colchester
events.text: Fairfax starved the Royalist garrison into surrender after eleven weeks.

events.name: Battle of Preston
events.text: Cromwell routed the larger Scottish and Royalist army.

events.name: Execution of Charles I
events.text: The King was beheaded and England became a republic, the Commonwealth.

steps.title: Cromwell in Ireland
steps.text: Ireland had been held since 1641 by Catholic Confederates, now allied with the Royalists under Ormond. Cromwell landed at Dublin in August 1649 after a Parliamentary victory at Rathmines, then stormed Drogheda and Wexford and massacred their garrisons and many townspeople. His campaign began a reconquest that confiscated most Catholic land.

events.name: Battle of Rathmines
events.text: The Dublin garrison routed Ormond's besieging army.

events.name: Siege of Drogheda
events.text: Cromwell stormed the town and his troops killed the garrison and many civilians.

events.name: Sack of Wexford
events.text: The town was taken and plundered during surrender talks.

steps.title: Dunbar and Worcester
steps.text: The Scots crowned Charles II, so Cromwell invaded Scotland and, though cornered at Dunbar, smashed David Leslie's army in September 1650. In 1651 Charles II led a Scottish army deep into England, but at Worcester, exactly a year after Dunbar, Cromwell destroyed it. Charles escaped to France after six weeks on the run, and England, Scotland and Ireland were ruled by Parliament and later by Cromwell as Lord Protector.

events.name: Battle of Dunbar
events.text: Cromwell's outnumbered army routed the Scots at dawn.

events.name: Battle of Worcester
events.text: The last battle of the civil wars destroyed Charles II's army.

events.name: Charles II escapes
events.text: After hiding in an oak tree, the young king sailed from Shoreham to France.

name: The Deluge: Khmelnytsky Uprising and the Swedish and Russian invasions of Poland-Lithuania
summary: In 1648 the Cossacks of Ukraine under Bohdan Khmelnytsky rose against the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, and when they placed themselves under the tsar in 1654 Russia invaded from the east, followed in 1655 by Sweden from the north and west. The Commonwealth nearly collapsed but recovered through national resistance and shifting alliances, ending the wars with the Peace of Oliva in 1660 and the Truce of Andrusovo in 1667. The Deluge cost Poland-Lithuania perhaps a third of its people and left Russia holding Smolensk, Kyiv and left-bank Ukraine.

steps.title: Khmelnytsky's uprising
steps.text: Bohdan Khmelnytsky, a Cossack officer wronged by a Polish magnate, rode out of the Zaporozhian Sich with Crimean Tatar allies. He destroyed the Polish crown armies at Zhovti Vody and Korsun, routed a noble levy at Pyliavtsi, and swept west to Lviv and Zamosc as peasants rose and Jews, Catholics and nobles were massacred across Ukraine.

events.name: Battle of Zhovti Vody
events.text: The Polish vanguard was surrounded and destroyed.

events.name: Battle of Korsun
events.text: Khmelnytsky ambushed the main crown army and captured both Polish hetmans.

events.name: Battle of Pyliavtsi
events.text: A huge Polish noble army fled in panic, opening the road west.

steps.title: Berestechko and stalemate
steps.text: King John II Casimir led the Commonwealth's full strength east and in 1651 won one of the largest battles of the century at Berestechko when the Tatar khan abandoned the Cossacks. Khmelnytsky recovered and annihilated a Polish army at Batih in 1652. Needing a stronger protector, he turned to Orthodox Moscow.

moves.commander: Bohdan Khmelnytsky and Islam III Giray
moves.label: Cossack and Tatar army

events.name: Battle of Berestechko
events.text: The Tatars fled and the Cossack camp was stormed, a crushing Polish victory.

events.name: Battle of Batih
events.text: Cossacks and Tatars destroyed a Polish army and massacred its prisoners.

steps.title: Russia invades
steps.text: At Pereiaslav in 1654 the Cossacks swore allegiance to Tsar Alexis, and Russia invaded the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Russian armies took Smolensk, Vitebsk, Mogilev and Minsk, and in August 1655 captured Vilnius, while Russians and Cossacks besieged Lviv in the south.

events.name: Pereiaslav Council
events.text: Khmelnytsky and the Cossack officers swore allegiance to the tsar.

events.name: Siege of Smolensk
events.text: Smolensk surrendered to the tsar after a three month siege.

events.name: Fall of Vilnius
events.text: The Lithuanian capital was taken, burned and looted.

steps.title: The Swedish Deluge
steps.text: In July 1655 Charles X Gustav of Sweden invaded from Pomerania and Livonia. The nobles of Greater Poland surrendered at Ujscie, the Lithuanian magnate Janusz Radziwill accepted Swedish rule, Warsaw and Krakow fell, and John II Casimir fled to Silesia. Only the monastery of Jasna Gora at Czestochowa held out, and its successful defence became a rallying cry.

events.name: Capitulation at Ujscie
events.text: The levy of Greater Poland surrendered without a fight and accepted Charles X Gustav.

events.name: Siege of Krakow
events.text: The old capital surrendered to the Swedes in October.

events.name: Siege of Jasna Gora
events.text: The Pauline monks and a small garrison beat off the Swedes, and the nation began to rise.

steps.title: The nation rises
steps.text: The king returned and Stefan Czarniecki waged a guerrilla war that wore down the Swedes, retaking Warsaw in June 1656. Charles X Gustav and the Elector of Brandenburg won it back in a three day battle, and in 1657 Prince Rakoczi of Transylvania invaded from the south. But Russia made a truce with Poland to fight Sweden, Denmark attacked Sweden, and in the Treaty of Wehlau Brandenburg switched sides in return for full sovereignty over Prussia.

moves.commander: Charles X Gustav and Frederick William
moves.label: Swedish and Brandenburg army

events.name: Battle of Warsaw
events.text: Swedish and Brandenburg troops beat a much larger Polish-Lithuanian army over three days.

events.name: Battle of Prostki
events.text: Lithuanian and Tatar cavalry routed a Swedish and Brandenburg force in Ducal Prussia.

events.name: Treaty of Wehlau
events.text: Brandenburg left Sweden for Poland in return for sovereignty over Prussia.

steps.title: Sweden turns away
steps.text: Charles X Gustav marched his army across the frozen Danish straits in 1658 and forced Denmark into a harsh peace, then attacked again, so Polish, Brandenburg and Austrian troops followed him to Denmark. In Ukraine the new hetman Ivan Vyhovsky rejoined Poland and beat a Russian army at Konotop. After Charles died, the Peace of Oliva in 1660 ended the war with Sweden, which kept Livonia.

moves.commander: Ivan Vyhovsky and the Crimean khan
moves.label: Cossacks and Tatars against Russia

events.name: March across the Belts
events.text: The Swedish army crossed the ice to Zealand and forced the Treaty of Roskilde on Denmark.

events.name: Battle of Konotop
events.text: Vyhovsky's Cossacks and the Crimean Tatars destroyed a Russian cavalry army.

events.name: Peace of Oliva
events.text: Poland gave up its claim to the Swedish throne and Livonia, ending the Swedish war.

steps.title: War with Russia and Andrusovo
steps.text: Freed from Sweden, the Commonwealth turned on Russia. Czarniecki and Sapieha beat Khovansky at Polonka, and Polish and Tatar forces trapped Sheremetev's army at Chudniv in 1660. But the exhausted Commonwealth could not win back the east, and the Truce of Andrusovo in 1667 split Ukraine along the Dnieper, giving Russia Smolensk, Kyiv and the left bank.

events.name: Battle of Polonka
events.text: Czarniecki and Sapieha routed Khovansky's Russian army in Lithuania.

events.name: Battle of Chudniv
events.text: Sheremetev's encircled Russian army surrendered.

events.name: Truce of Andrusovo
events.text: Russia kept Smolensk, Kyiv and Ukraine east of the Dnieper.

name: Great Turkish War
summary: The Ottoman grand vizier Kara Mustafa's siege of Vienna in 1683 was broken by a Polish and German relief army under Jan III Sobieski, and the Holy League of the Habsburgs, Poland, Venice and later Russia went on the offensive. Over sixteen years the allies took Buda, Belgrade for a time, the Morea and Azov, and Prince Eugene destroyed the Sultan's army at Zenta. The Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699 gave Hungary and Transylvania to Austria and marked the start of the Ottoman retreat from Europe.

steps.title: The siege of Vienna
steps.text: Backing a Hungarian revolt under Imre Thokoly, Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa led some 150,000 men up the Danube and besieged Vienna in July 1683. The city held for two months while Charles of Lorraine gathered a relief army. On 12 September King Jan III Sobieski led Polish and German troops down the Kahlenberg, and his winged hussars charged into the Ottoman camp in the largest cavalry charge in history.

events.name: Siege of Vienna
events.text: The garrison under Starhemberg held out for two months against mines and assaults.

events.name: Battle of Vienna
events.text: The relief army routed the besiegers; Kara Mustafa was later executed for his failure.

steps.title: Holy League and Buda
steps.text: Pope Innocent XI brought the Emperor, Poland and Venice together in the Holy League in 1684. Charles of Lorraine pushed down the Danube and in 1686, after a long siege, stormed Buda, the Ottoman capital of Hungary for 145 years. In the south the Venetian fleet under Francesco Morosini landed in Greece and conquered the Morea.

events.name: Holy League formed
events.text: The Emperor, Poland and Venice allied under the pope against the Ottomans.

events.name: Siege of Buda
events.text: The Habsburg army stormed Buda after 78 days.

events.name: Fall of Nafplio
events.text: Morosini took the main Ottoman fortress of the Morea.

steps.title: Mohacs and Belgrade
steps.text: At the second battle of Mohacs in 1687 Lorraine and Max Emanuel of Bavaria routed the grand vizier's army; the defeat led to a mutiny that deposed Sultan Mehmed IV. Transylvania submitted to the Habsburgs, a Venetian shell blew up the Parthenon in Athens, and in 1688 Max Emanuel stormed Belgrade.

events.name: Battle of Mohacs
events.text: The imperial victory near Mount Harsany avenged the disaster of 1526.

events.name: Parthenon destroyed
events.text: A Venetian mortar round ignited the Ottoman powder store inside the Parthenon.

events.name: Siege of Belgrade
events.text: Max Emanuel stormed the key fortress on the Danube.

steps.title: Ottoman revival
steps.text: France attacked the Rhine in 1688, drawing Habsburg troops west. Louis of Baden still pushed deep into Serbia to Nis and Vidin, but the able grand vizier Fazil Mustafa Pasha struck back in 1690, retaking Nis and Belgrade as tens of thousands of Serbs fled north with their patriarch. At Slankamen in 1691 Louis of Baden beat the Ottomans and Fazil Mustafa was killed, fixing the front on the Sava and Danube.

events.name: Battle of Nis
events.text: Louis of Baden defeated the Ottomans and took Nis.

events.name: Recapture of Belgrade
events.text: Fazil Mustafa retook Belgrade when its powder magazine exploded.

events.name: Battle of Slankamen
events.text: A bloody imperial victory in which the grand vizier was killed.

steps.title: Azov and Zenta
steps.text: Sultan Mustafa II took the field himself and won back ground in the Banat. Russia, in the League since 1686, struck at the Black Sea, and in 1696 the young Peter the Great took Azov with a new river fleet. In September 1697 Prince Eugene of Savoy caught the Sultan's army crossing the Tisza at Zenta and destroyed it while Mustafa watched from the far bank.

events.name: Siege of Azov
events.text: Peter's galleys cut the fortress off from the sea and it surrendered.

events.name: Battle of Zenta
events.text: Eugene attacked the Ottoman army as it crossed the Tisza, killing tens of thousands.

steps.title: Karlowitz
steps.text: Exhausted, the Ottomans accepted British and Dutch mediation. At Karlowitz in January 1699 they ceded Hungary and Transylvania to Austria, the Morea and much of Dalmatia to Venice and Podolia to Poland, and in 1700 Russia's envoy, sailing to Constantinople on a Russian warship, secured Azov. It was the first time the Ottomans had signed away large European lands.

moves.label: Russian envoy aboard the warship Krepost

events.name: Treaty of Karlowitz
events.text: Austria gained Hungary and Transylvania, Venice the Morea and Poland Podolia.

events.name: Treaty of Constantinople
events.text: The Ottomans ceded Azov to Russia.

name: Great Northern War
summary: Russia, Denmark-Norway and Saxony-Poland attacked the Swedish Empire in 1700, expecting an easy win over its teenage king Charles XII. Charles beat each in turn but lost his army deep in Ukraine at Poltava in 1709, and while he sat in Ottoman exile Peter the Great took the Baltic provinces and Finland. The Treaty of Nystad in 1721 ended Sweden's age as a great power and made Russia an empire and the master of the Baltic.

sides.name: Russia, Denmark-Norway, Saxony-Poland and later Prussia and Hanover

steps.title: Copenhagen and Narva
steps.text: Denmark, Saxony and Russia attacked at once. Eighteen-year-old Charles XII landed beside Copenhagen and forced Denmark out of the war within weeks, then shipped his army to Estonia. In a November snowstorm at Narva about 10,000 Swedes broke Peter the Great's besieging army of over 30,000.

events.name: Treaty of Travendal
events.text: Denmark made peace after Charles threatened Copenhagen.

events.name: Battle of Narva
events.text: The Swedes attacked in a blizzard and routed the Russian army.

steps.title: Charles in Poland, Peter on the Neva
steps.text: Charles turned on Augustus II, crossing the Daugava at Riga, taking Warsaw and beating the Saxons and Poles at Kliszow. He had Augustus deposed in Poland, and after Rehnskiold's victory at Fraustadt he invaded Saxony and forced Augustus out of the war at Altranstadt in 1706. Meanwhile Peter rebuilt his army, took Ingria and founded St Petersburg at the mouth of the Neva in 1703.

moves.label: Swedish campaign in Poland and Saxony

events.name: Battle of Kliszow
events.text: Charles routed a larger Saxon and Polish army.

events.name: St Petersburg founded
events.text: Peter began his new capital and Baltic port on land taken from Sweden.

events.name: Battle of Fraustadt
events.text: Rehnskiold destroyed a Saxon and Russian army twice his size.

steps.title: The march on Moscow and Poltava
steps.text: In 1708 Charles marched east from Saxony toward Moscow, winning at Holowczyn, but the Russians burned the land before him. Peter destroyed Lewenhaupt's supply column at Lesnaya, and Charles turned south into Ukraine, where the Cossack hetman Mazepa joined him. After a terrible winter the Swedes attacked Peter's fortified camp at Poltava in June 1709 and were crushed; the rest of the army surrendered at Perevolochna and Charles fled to Ottoman Bender.

events.name: Battle of Lesnaya
events.text: Peter destroyed the Swedish supply train before it could reach Charles.

events.name: Battle of Poltava
events.text: The Swedish army was shattered and Rehnskiold captured.

events.name: Surrender at Perevolochna
events.text: Some 14,000 Swedes trapped on the Dnieper laid down their arms.

steps.title: Russia takes the Baltic and Finland
steps.text: With Sweden's field army gone, Russia took Riga, Reval and Vyborg in 1710, and Denmark and Saxony rejoined the war. Peter was nearly destroyed when an Ottoman army trapped him on the Pruth in 1711 and had to give back Azov. He then turned to Finland, and in 1714 his galley fleet beat the Swedish navy at Gangut, the first great Russian naval victory.

moves.label: Galley fleet along the Finnish coast

events.name: Siege of Riga
events.text: Riga surrendered after a siege ravaged by plague.

events.name: Pruth campaign
events.text: Surrounded by a huge Ottoman army, Peter bought his way out by returning Azov.

events.name: Battle of Gangut
events.text: Russian galleys outflanked becalmed Swedish warships off Hanko.

steps.title: Charles returns and falls
steps.text: Charles rode across Europe from Bender to Stralsund in 1714, but Prussia and Hanover joined his enemies and Stralsund fell in 1715, ending Sweden's hold on Germany. Charles raised a new army and invaded Norway to strike Denmark, and in December 1718 he was shot dead in the trenches before Fredriksten fortress.

moves.commander: Frederick William I and Frederick IV
moves.label: Prussian and Danish siege army

events.name: Siege of Stralsund
events.text: Prussians, Danes and Saxons took Sweden's last major German fortress.

events.name: Death of Charles XII
events.text: The king was killed by a shot to the head while inspecting siege works at Fredriksten.

steps.title: Nystad and the Russian Empire
steps.text: Sweden made peace with Hanover, Prussia and Denmark, but Russian galleys raided and burned the Swedish coast close to Stockholm in 1719 to 1721 and won again at Grengam. By the Treaty of Nystad Sweden ceded Livonia, Estonia, Ingria and part of Karelia to Russia, and Peter was proclaimed Emperor of All Russia.

moves.label: Galley raids on the Swedish coast

events.name: Battle of Grengam
events.text: Russian galleys captured four Swedish frigates in the Aland islands.

events.name: Treaty of Nystad
events.text: Sweden ceded its eastern Baltic provinces to Russia.

events.name: Peter proclaimed emperor
events.text: The Senate gave Peter the titles Emperor and the Great, founding the Russian Empire.

name: War of the Spanish Succession
summary: When the childless Charles II of Spain left his empire to Louis XIV's grandson Philip, England, the Dutch Republic and Austria formed a Grand Alliance to stop France and Spain from uniting. Marlborough and Prince Eugene won great victories at Blenheim, Ramillies, Turin and Oudenarde, but Philip V held Spain with French help. The Treaties of Utrecht and Rastatt in 1713 to 1714 left Philip king of Spain while Austria took Spain's European lands and Britain gained Gibraltar, setting the balance of power for the century.

steps.title: A Bourbon on the Spanish throne
steps.text: Charles II of Spain died in 1700 leaving everything to Louis XIV's grandson, who became Philip V. Austria claimed the inheritance for Archduke Charles, and Prince Eugene crossed the Alps to attack Spanish Milan, winning at Carpi and Chiari. England and the Dutch joined Austria in a Grand Alliance and declared war in 1702, and an Anglo-Dutch fleet destroyed the Spanish treasure fleet in Vigo Bay.

moves.label: French and Spanish army of Italy

events.name: Philip V enters Madrid
events.text: Louis XIV's grandson was received as king of Spain.

events.name: Battle of Chiari
events.text: Eugene repulsed the French and Spanish assault on his entrenched camp.

events.name: Battle of Vigo Bay
events.text: The allies destroyed the French escort and the Spanish treasure fleet.

steps.title: Blenheim and Gibraltar
steps.text: Bavaria had joined France, and in 1704 a Franco-Bavarian army threatened Vienna. Marlborough marched his army 400 kilometres from the Low Countries to the Danube, joined Prince Eugene, and at Blenheim destroyed the army of Marshal Tallard, saving Austria. Portugal and Savoy had switched to the allies in 1703, and in August 1704 an Anglo-Dutch fleet took Gibraltar.

moves.label: French army through the Black Forest

events.name: Battle of Blenheim
events.text: Marlborough and Eugene destroyed the Franco-Bavarian army and captured Tallard.

events.name: Capture of Gibraltar
events.text: Anglo-Dutch marines took the Rock, which Britain still holds.

steps.title: Year of victories: Ramillies and Turin
steps.text: In May 1706 Marlborough routed Villeroi at Ramillies and the Spanish Netherlands fell to the allies within weeks. In September Prince Eugene marched along the Po and relieved besieged Turin, driving the French from Italy. From Portugal, Galway's allied army even entered Madrid for a few months, proclaiming Archduke Charles king.

moves.label: Allied army from Portugal to Madrid

events.name: Battle of Ramillies
events.text: Marlborough's victory cost France the Spanish Netherlands.

events.name: Battle of Turin
events.text: Eugene and Victor Amadeus broke the French siege and France lost northern Italy.

events.name: Allies take Madrid
events.text: Archduke Charles was proclaimed king, but Castile rejected him.

steps.title: Almansa, Oudenarde and Malplaquet
steps.text: In Spain Berwick crushed Galway's allied army at Almansa in 1707, securing most of the country for Philip V. In the north Marlborough and Eugene beat the French at Oudenarde in 1708 and took Lille. After the Great Frost of 1709 Louis XIV sought peace, but refused the allies' harsh terms, and at Malplaquet Villars lost the field at such cost to the allies that France was saved from invasion.

events.name: Battle of Almansa
events.text: Berwick's victory restored Valencia and Aragon to Philip V.

events.name: Battle of Oudenarde
events.text: Marlborough and Eugene beat Vendome and went on to take Lille.

events.name: Battle of Malplaquet
events.text: The bloodiest battle of the century; the allies won the field but lost a quarter of their men.

steps.title: The tide turns: Brihuega and Denain
steps.text: Stanhope and Starhemberg took Madrid again in 1710, but Vendome trapped the British at Brihuega and fought the allies to a standstill at Villaviciosa, deciding the war in Spain. In 1711 Archduke Charles became emperor, and Britain, unwilling to see Austria and Spain united, opened secret talks with France. Without British troops, Eugene was beaten by Villars at Denain in 1712.

events.name: Brihuega and Villaviciosa
events.text: Vendome captured Stanhope's British corps and drove the allies from Castile.

events.name: Emperor Joseph I dies
events.text: Archduke Charles inherited the Austrian lands and the imperial crown.

events.name: Battle of Denain
events.text: Villars crushed Eugene's Dutch rearguard, saving France.

steps.title: Utrecht and Rastatt
steps.text: The Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 recognised Philip V as king of Spain on condition that the French and Spanish crowns never unite. Austria took Spain's Netherlands, Milan, Naples and Sardinia, Savoy gained Sicily, and Britain kept Gibraltar and Minorca and won trading rights in Spanish America. The emperor made peace at Rastatt in 1714, and Philip's army took Barcelona that September.

events.name: Treaty of Utrecht
events.text: Philip V kept Spain but gave up its European lands and his claim to France.

events.name: Treaty of Rastatt
events.text: The emperor accepted the settlement and took the Spanish Netherlands and Italian lands.

events.name: Siege of Barcelona
events.text: Barcelona fell to Berwick after a 14 month siege, ending Catalan self-government.

name: Nader Shah's Campaigns
summary: Nader, a Turkmen soldier of the Afshar tribe, rescued Persia from Afghan occupation, drove out the Ottomans and Russians, made himself shah in 1736 and then struck east, sacking Delhi in 1739 and subduing the Uzbek khanates. His wars made Persia briefly the strongest power in Asia, but the cost and his growing cruelty led to his murder in 1747, after which his empire fell apart and Ahmad Shah Durrani founded the Afghan state.

steps.label: 1729 to 1730
steps.title: Driving out the Afghans
steps.text: Since 1722 Ghilzai Afghans had held Isfahan, while Ottomans and Russians carved up western and northern Persia. Nader, now commanding for the exiled Safavid Tahmasp II, marched west from Mashhad, beat Ashraf's Afghans at Damghan and Murcheh Khort and retook Isfahan, then chased them south past Shiraz until their army dissolved.

events.name: Battle of Damghan
events.text: Nader's disciplined musketeers and artillery broke Ashraf's Afghan army in its first clash.

events.name: Battle of Murcheh Khort
events.text: A second defeat forced the Afghans to abandon Isfahan, ending seven years of occupation.

steps.label: 1730 to 1735
steps.title: War with the Ottomans
steps.text: Nader swung west and retook Hamadan and Tabriz, but Tahmasp lost them again while Nader was away, so Nader deposed him in 1732 and ruled as regent for the infant Abbas III. Beaten outside Baghdad by Topal Osman Pasha in 1733, he rebuilt his army in months and killed Osman near Kirkuk. In 1735 he destroyed the main Ottoman army at Yeghevard and recovered the Caucasus, while Russia handed back the Caspian provinces.

events.name: Battle of Kirkuk
events.text: Nader avenged his defeat at Samarra months earlier, and Topal Osman Pasha was killed.

events.name: Battle of Yeghevard
events.text: Nader routed a much larger Ottoman army near Yerevan and won back Armenia and Georgia.

steps.label: 1736 to 1738
steps.title: Nader becomes shah and turns east
steps.text: At a great assembly on the Mughan plain in 1736 Nader had himself proclaimed shah, ending the Safavid dynasty. He then led perhaps 80,000 men east against the Hotaki Afghans of Kandahar, starved the city out in a year long siege, and pressed on to take Kabul from its Mughal governor.

events.name: Nader crowned on the Mughan plain
events.text: An assembly of notables accepted Nader as shah, founding the Afsharid dynasty.

events.name: Siege of Kandahar
events.text: The last Hotaki stronghold fell after a year, and many Afghans joined Nader's army.

steps.label: 1738 to 1739
steps.title: The sack of Delhi
steps.text: Using the shelter given to Afghan fugitives as a pretext, Nader forced the Khyber Pass, took Lahore and met the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah's far larger army at Karnal, where his cavalry and musketeers won in a few hours. In Delhi a riot against his troops led to a massacre of perhaps 20,000 people, and he carried home the Peacock Throne, the Koh-i-Noor diamond and treasure worth years of Persian taxes.

events.name: Battle of Karnal
events.text: Nader shattered the Mughal army in about three hours and captured the emperor.

events.name: Sack of Delhi
events.text: Persian troops massacred thousands and looted the Mughal treasury, a blow from which the empire never recovered.

steps.title: Bukhara and Khiva
steps.text: Returning from India, Nader crossed the Oxus with artillery and treasure-fed troops. Abul Fayz Khan of Bukhara submitted without a fight, while Ilbars Khan of Khiva resisted, was defeated and executed, and thousands of Persian slaves held in Khiva were freed.

events.name: Submission of Bukhara
events.text: The khan of Bukhara accepted Persian overlordship and gave the lands south of the Oxus.

events.name: Fall of Khiva
events.text: Nader's army took Khiva, executed its khan and freed captives held there.

steps.label: 1741 to 1746
steps.title: Overreach in Dagestan and Mesopotamia
steps.text: Nader's campaign against the mountain peoples of Dagestan bogged down in guerrilla war, and after an attempt on his life he had his own son Reza Qoli blinded. A second Ottoman war brought failed sieges of Mosul and Kars, but a crushing victory near Kars in 1745 led to the Treaty of Kerden, which restored the old frontier of 1639.

events.name: Siege of Mosul
events.text: The Ottoman garrison held out for weeks against heavy bombardment and Nader withdrew.

events.name: Battle of Kars
events.text: Nader destroyed Yegen Mehmed Pasha's army, his last great victory.

steps.title: Murder and collapse
steps.text: Increasingly suspicious and brutal, Nader taxed his realm into revolt and executed officials and kin. In June 1747 a group of his own officers killed him in his tent near Quchan. His empire broke apart within months: his Afghan commander Ahmad Shah Durrani rode off with the treasury guard and founded the Durrani Empire, while Persia sank into civil war.

events.name: Assassination of Nader Shah
events.text: Nader was killed by his own officers at Fathabad, near Quchan.

name: Seven Years' War
summary: A colonial clash in the Ohio Country in 1754 merged with Austria's attempt to win back Silesia from Prussia into a war fought across Europe, North America, the Caribbean, Africa and India. Britain and Prussia faced France, Austria, Russia, Sweden and later Spain; Frederick the Great survived, and Britain took New France, Florida and dominance in India. The war made Britain the leading global power, and its debts helped spark the American and French revolutions.

steps.label: 1754 to 1755
steps.title: War begins in the Ohio Country
steps.text: Britain and France both claimed the Ohio valley. A young George Washington, sent to challenge the French Fort Duquesne, was forced to surrender at Fort Necessity in 1754. The next year General Braddock's British regulars marched on the fort and were ambushed and routed by French troops and their Native allies at the Monongahela.

events.name: Fort Necessity
events.text: Washington's Virginians surrendered to a French and Native force.

events.name: Battle of the Monongahela
events.text: Braddock was mortally wounded and his column cut to pieces near Fort Duquesne.

steps.label: 1756 to 1757
steps.title: Frederick's year of battles
steps.text: Austria, France and Russia allied to dismember Prussia, so Frederick struck first, overrunning Saxony in 1756. In 1757 he was beaten at Kolin in Bohemia as French, Imperial, Russian and Swedish armies closed in, but he marched west to rout a Franco-Imperial army at Rossbach, then raced east to crush the Austrians at Leuthen and save Silesia.

moves.label: West to Rossbach, east to Leuthen

events.name: Battle of Kolin
events.text: Daun's Austrians repulsed Frederick, ending his invasion of Bohemia.

events.name: Battle of Rossbach
events.text: Frederick routed a Franco-Imperial army twice his size in about ninety minutes.

events.name: Battle of Leuthen
events.text: Frederick's oblique attack shattered the Austrians and recovered Silesia.

steps.label: 1757 to 1761
steps.title: The struggle for India
steps.text: Robert Clive's East India Company troops retook Calcutta and, with the Nawab's commanders bribed to stand aside, defeated Siraj ud-Daulah at Plassey, putting Bengal under Company control. In the south Eyre Coote beat the French under Lally at Wandiwash and took Pondicherry, ending French hopes of an Indian empire.

events.name: Battle of Plassey
events.text: Clive defeated Siraj ud-Daulah when key Bengali commanders held back, giving the Company Bengal.

events.name: Battle of Wandiwash
events.text: Coote decisively defeated Lally's French army in the Carnatic.

events.name: Siege of Pondicherry
events.text: The main French base in India surrendered after a long siege.

steps.title: Pitt's war for North America
steps.text: William Pitt poured British troops and ships into America while paying Prussia to hold the line in Europe. An amphibious force under Amherst took Louisbourg and opened the St Lawrence, and Forbes forced the French to abandon Fort Duquesne, but Montcalm bloodily repulsed Abercrombie's huge army at Fort Carillon.

events.name: Siege of Louisbourg
events.text: British forces took the great French fortress on Cape Breton Island after seven weeks.

events.name: Battle of Carillon
events.text: Montcalm's outnumbered French beat off repeated British assaults at Ticonderoga.

steps.title: The year of victories
steps.text: Britain's annus mirabilis: Wolfe sailed up the St Lawrence and took Quebec in a battle that killed both him and Montcalm, Ferdinand of Brunswick beat the French at Minden, and Hawke destroyed a French fleet at Quiberon Bay, ending invasion plans. Prussia meanwhile was nearly destroyed by Russians and Austrians at Kunersdorf.

events.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
events.text: Wolfe's army defeated Montcalm outside Quebec, which surrendered days later.

events.name: Battle of Minden
events.text: British and German infantry broke the French cavalry and saved Hanover.

events.name: Battle of Quiberon Bay
events.text: Hawke chased the French fleet into a rocky bay in a gale and wrecked it.

steps.label: 1760 to 1761
steps.title: Canada falls, Prussia at bay
steps.text: Three British armies converged on Montreal, and the French governor surrendered all of New France in September 1760. In Europe a Russian raid briefly took Berlin and Frederick, his armies bled white, won a costly victory at Torgau, but by 1761 Prussia was close to collapse.

moves.label: Down the St Lawrence from Oswego

events.name: Surrender of Montreal
events.text: Vaudreuil capitulated, handing all of New France to Britain.

events.name: Battle of Torgau
events.text: Frederick beat Daun at terrible cost and kept Saxony.

steps.title: Miracle of the House of Brandenburg
steps.text: Empress Elizabeth's death in January 1762 brought the pro-Prussian Peter III to the throne; Russia, then Sweden, made peace. Spain entered the war on France's side and paid dearly: British expeditions captured Havana and Manila, and a Spanish invasion of Portugal was beaten back.

events.name: Siege of Havana
events.text: Britain took Spain's key Caribbean port after a two-month siege.

events.name: Fall of Manila
events.text: A British force from India stormed the capital of the Spanish Philippines.

events.name: Battle of Freiberg
events.text: Prince Henry of Prussia beat the Austrians in the last big battle in Germany.

steps.title: Peace of Paris and Hubertusburg
steps.text: The Treaty of Paris gave Britain Canada, Florida and everything east of the Mississippi, and confirmed its lead in India; Havana and Manila went back to Spain, and France ceded Louisiana west of the river to Spain. Days later Prussia and Austria signed peace at Hubertusburg, leaving Silesia with Prussia and the map of Europe unchanged.

events.name: Treaty of Paris
events.text: France gave up New France and Britain became the leading colonial power.

events.name: Treaty of Hubertusburg
events.text: Austria accepted Prussian possession of Silesia.

name: Qing Conquest of Dzungaria
summary: The Qianlong Emperor exploited a succession struggle in the Dzungar Khanate, the last great nomad empire of the steppe, to send armies west in 1755. When his ally Amursana turned against him, Qianlong ordered the Dzungars destroyed; war, massacre and smallpox killed most of their people by 1758. The conquest, completed in the Tarim Basin in 1759, added Xinjiang to the Qing Empire and ended the age of steppe empires.

steps.label: Spring 1755
steps.title: Qing armies march on Ili
steps.text: Civil war over the Dzungar throne drove the noble Amursana to seek Qing help against khan Dawachi. Qianlong sent two columns west, Bandi's from Uliastai with Amursana as deputy and another from Barkol. Many Dzungar clans submitted, Ili fell without a major battle, and Dawachi fled over the Tian Shan, where a local beg handed him over at Uch Turpan.

events.name: Qing take Ili
events.text: The Dzungar capital fell almost unopposed as clans went over to the Qing.

events.name: Capture of Dawachi
events.text: The fleeing khan was seized at Uch Turpan and sent to Beijing.

steps.label: Autumn 1755 to 1756
steps.title: Amursana's revolt
steps.text: Amursana had hoped to rule the Dzungars himself; when Qianlong instead split them into four vassal khanates, he revolted. Most Qing troops had already gone home, and the small garrison at Ili was overwhelmed, its commander Bandi killing himself. A Qing counter-attack in 1756 drove Amursana into the Kazakh steppe, while a Mongol rebellion in Khalkha distracted the Qing.

events.name: Fall of the Ili garrison
events.text: Amursana's men overran the Qing post and Bandi took his own life.

steps.title: Extermination
steps.text: Qianlong ordered that the Dzungars be wiped out. Zhaohui and Fude swept the land from the Altai to the Ili, killing men and enslaving women and children, while a smallpox epidemic tore through the survivors. Amursana fled to Russian Siberia and died of smallpox at Tobolsk. Most of a Dzungar population of perhaps 600,000 perished or fled.

events.name: Dzungar genocide
events.text: Qing massacres, famine and smallpox destroyed the Dzungar people as a nation.

events.name: Death of Amursana
events.text: The last Dzungar leader died of smallpox in Russian Tobolsk.

steps.label: 1758 to 1759
steps.title: Xinjiang: the Tarim Basin falls
steps.text: With Dzungaria emptied, the Khoja brothers who ruled the oasis cities of the Tarim Basin defied the Qing. Zhaohui besieged Kucha, was himself trapped for months at Yarkand at the Black Water Camp, but was relieved and took Kashgar and Yarkand in 1759. The Khojas fled to Badakhshan, where they were killed, and the whole region became the Qing 'New Frontier', Xinjiang.

moves.label: Qing army into the Tarim Basin

events.name: Siege of Kucha
events.text: The oasis fell after a long siege, though Khoja Jahan escaped.

events.name: Black Water Camp
events.text: Zhaohui held out for three months near Yarkand until relief arrived.

events.name: Fall of Kashgar
events.text: Kashgar and Yarkand submitted and the Tarim Basin passed to the Qing.

name: Afghan-Maratha War
summary: As Mughal power collapsed, the Hindu Maratha Confederacy pushed north to the Indus, colliding with Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan empire, which claimed the Punjab. Durrani, backed by the Rohilla Najib ad-Dawla and the Nawab of Oudh, trapped the main Maratha army at Panipat and destroyed it in January 1761, one of the bloodiest battles of the century. Neither victor could hold north India, opening the way for the Sikhs in the Punjab and the British East India Company.

steps.title: The Marathas reach the Indus
steps.text: Invited in by the Mughal court's factions, a Maratha army under Raghunathrao and Malhar Rao Holkar swept through the Punjab, took Sirhind and Lahore and drove out Ahmad Shah's son Timur Shah. Maratha outposts at Attock and Peshawar marked the furthest reach of their power, and a direct challenge to Durrani.

events.name: Maratha capture of Lahore
events.text: Timur Shah's Afghan garrison fled and the Punjab passed to the Marathas.

steps.label: Late 1759 to 1760
steps.title: Ahmad Shah strikes back
steps.text: Ahmad Shah crossed the Indus with a large army, swept the thin Maratha garrisons out of the Punjab and joined the Rohilla chief Najib ad-Dawla. North of Delhi he caught Dattaji Shinde at Barari Ghat, where Dattaji was killed, then routed Holkar and camped at Anupshahr on the Ganges, winning over the Nawab of Oudh.

events.name: Battle of Barari Ghat
events.text: Dattaji Shinde was killed as the Afghans crossed the Yamuna north of Delhi.

steps.title: Bhau marches north
steps.text: The Peshwa sent his cousin Sadashivrao Bhau north with the Maratha field army, French-trained artillery under Ibrahim Khan Gardi and a huge train of pilgrims and followers. Bhau took Delhi and stormed the Afghan post at Kunjpura, but Ahmad Shah crossed the Yamuna at Baghpat behind him, cutting the Marathas off from Delhi and the south. Bhau dug in at Panipat.

events.name: Capture of Delhi
events.text: Bhau seized the Mughal capital and stripped the Red Fort to pay his troops.

events.name: Storming of Kunjpura
events.text: The Marathas destroyed the Afghan garrison and seized its grain stores.

steps.label: 14 Jan 1761
steps.title: The Third Battle of Panipat
steps.text: After two months of blockade the starving Marathas attacked. Ibrahim Khan Gardi's guns and Bhau's centre at first drove back the Afghans, but Ahmad Shah threw in his reserves and camel-mounted swivel guns, and by afternoon the Maratha army broke. Bhau and the Peshwa's heir Vishwasrao were killed, and tens of thousands of soldiers and camp followers were slaughtered in the rout.

events.name: Third Battle of Panipat
events.text: The Maratha field army was destroyed in one of the largest battles of the 18th century.

steps.label: 1761 and after
steps.title: A victory without a prize
steps.text: With his own troops unpaid and restless, Ahmad Shah went home to Kabul within weeks, leaving north India to his allies and to the rising Sikhs in the Punjab. The Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao died months later. The Marathas recovered under Madhavrao and returned to Delhi in 1771, but Panipat had checked them just as the East India Company was expanding from Bengal.

events.name: Death of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao
events.text: The Maratha leader died in Pune, reportedly broken by the news of Panipat.

name: American Revolutionary War
summary: Thirteen British colonies rebelled against Parliament's taxes and authority, declared independence in 1776 and fought Britain, its Loyalists and German auxiliaries. After the victory at Saratoga brought France, then Spain and the Dutch Republic, into the war, a Franco-American army and French fleet trapped Cornwallis at Yorktown. The Treaty of Paris recognised the United States, whose republic inspired revolutions in France and Latin America.

steps.title: Lexington, Bunker Hill and Canada
steps.text: British regulars marching from Boston to seize militia arms at Concord were driven back by swarms of colonial militia, who then besieged Boston. The British took Bunker Hill only at a terrible cost. Congress made George Washington commander of a new Continental Army and sent two forces north, under Montgomery and Arnold, which failed in a snowstorm assault on Quebec.

events.name: Lexington and Concord
events.text: Militia drove the British column back to Boston, opening the war.

events.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
events.text: The British took the heights but lost over a thousand men killed or wounded.

events.name: Assault on Quebec
events.text: Montgomery was killed and Arnold wounded in a failed night attack.

steps.title: Independence and the fight for New York
steps.text: Cannon hauled from Ticonderoga forced the British out of Boston in March. Congress declared independence on 4 July just as the largest British expedition of the century landed at New York. Howe drove Washington from Long Island, Manhattan and New Jersey, but on the night of 25 December Washington crossed the Delaware and captured the Hessian garrison at Trenton.

moves.label: Fleet from Halifax to New York

events.name: Declaration of Independence
events.text: Congress in Philadelphia declared the colonies free and independent states.

events.name: Battle of Long Island
events.text: Howe outflanked Washington's army in Brooklyn in the largest battle of the war.

events.name: Battle of Trenton
events.text: Washington's surprise attack revived the flagging revolution.

steps.title: Saratoga
steps.text: Burgoyne pushed south from Canada down Lake Champlain to cut New England off, while Howe sailed instead to the Chesapeake and took Philadelphia after beating Washington at Brandywine. Burgoyne, isolated in the wilderness of upstate New York, was surrounded by Gates's swelling army and surrendered his whole force at Saratoga.

events.name: Battle of Brandywine
events.text: Howe flanked Washington and opened the road to Philadelphia.

events.name: Battles of Saratoga
events.text: Gates and Arnold defeated Burgoyne, whose surrender brought France into the war.

steps.label: 1778 to 1779
steps.title: A world war
steps.text: France signed an alliance with the United States in February 1778, and Spain joined France in 1779, laying siege to Gibraltar. Washington's army, drilled at Valley Forge, fought the British to a draw at Monmouth as they pulled back from Philadelphia to New York, where the northern war settled into stalemate. Britain turned south, taking Savannah and beating off a Franco-American attempt to retake it.

fronts.label: American lines around British New York

events.name: Franco-American alliance
events.text: France recognised the United States and went to war with Britain.

events.name: Battle of Monmouth
events.text: A long, hot battle ended in a draw but showed the Continental Army's new discipline.

events.name: Siege of Savannah
events.text: British defenders repulsed a bloody French and American assault.

steps.label: 1780 to early 1781
steps.title: The war in the South
steps.text: Clinton captured Charleston with its entire American garrison, and Cornwallis routed Gates at Camden. But backcountry militia destroyed a Loyalist force at Kings Mountain, and Washington's best general, Nathanael Greene, wore Cornwallis down: Morgan won at Cowpens and Greene's army survived Guilford Courthouse, leaving the British too weak to hold the Carolinas.

events.name: Siege of Charleston
events.text: Some 5,000 American troops surrendered, the worst American defeat of the war.

events.name: Battle of Kings Mountain
events.text: Patriot frontier militia wiped out Cornwallis's Loyalist flank force.

events.name: Battle of Cowpens
events.text: Daniel Morgan's double envelopment destroyed Tarleton's British legion.

steps.label: Sep to Oct 1781
steps.title: Yorktown
steps.text: Cornwallis marched into Virginia and fortified Yorktown to await the Royal Navy. Washington and Rochambeau slipped away from New York and marched south, while de Grasse's French fleet sailed up from the Caribbean and beat off the British fleet off the Virginia Capes. Trapped by land and sea, Cornwallis surrendered his army on 19 October.

events.name: Battle of the Chesapeake
events.text: De Grasse's fleet drove off Graves and sealed Cornwallis off from rescue.

events.name: Siege of Yorktown
events.text: Cornwallis surrendered some 8,000 men, effectively ending the war in America.

steps.label: 1782 to 1783
steps.title: The Saintes, Gibraltar and peace
steps.text: The war went on at sea and overseas: Rodney smashed de Grasse's fleet at the Saintes, saving Jamaica, and the great Franco-Spanish assault on Gibraltar failed. With no hope of reconquering America, Britain made peace. The Treaty of Paris of September 1783 recognised the United States with borders reaching the Mississippi.

events.name: Battle of the Saintes
events.text: Rodney broke the French line and captured de Grasse.

events.name: Great Siege of Gibraltar
events.text: The British garrison destroyed the floating batteries of the grand assault.

events.name: Treaty of Paris
events.text: Britain recognised the independence of the United States.

name: Rebellion of Tupac Amaru II
summary: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, a mestizo cacique claiming Inca descent as Tupac Amaru II, rose against abusive Spanish officials and forced labour in the Andes in 1780. The revolt, joined in Upper Peru by Tupac Katari's siege of La Paz, drew in tens of thousands of Indigenous people before Spanish armies crushed it, with perhaps 100,000 dead. It was the largest colonial uprising in Spanish America before the wars of independence and led Spain to suppress Inca symbols and reform colonial rule.

steps.label: Nov 1780
steps.title: Revolt at Tinta
steps.text: On 4 November 1780 Tupac Amaru seized the hated corregidor Antonio de Arriaga, and six days later hanged him before a crowd at Tungasuca. Calling for an end to the forced labour and forced sales of goods, he raised thousands of followers, and on 18 November they destroyed a Spanish militia column from Cusco at Sangarara.

events.name: Execution of Arriaga
events.text: The hanging of the corregidor at Tungasuca launched the rebellion.

events.name: Battle of Sangarara
events.text: Rebels destroyed the Spanish column in the burning church where it sheltered.

steps.label: Dec 1780 to Jan 1781
steps.title: Siege of Cusco
steps.text: Rather than strike Cusco at once, Tupac Amaru marched south to raise the provinces around Lake Titicaca, while his wife Micaela Bastidas organised supplies and urged a swift attack. When he finally besieged Cusco in early January, loyal Indigenous troops and reinforcements from Lima had arrived, and after days of fighting he withdrew.

events.name: Siege of Cusco
events.text: The city held, and the rebels lost the chance of a quick victory.

steps.label: Feb to May 1781
steps.title: Capture and execution
steps.text: José del Valle led some 15,000 troops, many of them Indigenous auxiliaries, south from Cusco. The rebels were beaten near Tinta and Tupac Amaru was betrayed and captured at Langui in April. On 18 May in Cusco's main square, after watching the execution of his wife and son, he was torn by horses and beheaded.

events.name: Capture at Langui
events.text: Betrayed by his own officers, Tupac Amaru was seized with his family.

events.name: Execution in Cusco
events.text: Spanish authorities executed Tupac Amaru, Micaela Bastidas and their followers.

steps.label: Mar to Oct 1781
steps.title: Tupac Katari besieges La Paz
steps.text: In Upper Peru the Aymara leader Julian Apaza, calling himself Tupac Katari, ringed La Paz with some 40,000 men for over six months, and the city lost perhaps a third of its people to hunger. Andres Tupac Amaru took Sorata by flooding it. Columns under Ignacio Flores and then José de Reseguin finally broke the siege in October.

fronts.label: Rebel siege ring around La Paz

moves.label: Aymara forces close on La Paz

events.name: Siege of La Paz
events.text: The city held out from March to October until relieved.

events.name: Fall of Sorata
events.text: Rebels dammed a stream and flooded the town, killing much of its population.

steps.label: Nov 1781 to 1783
steps.title: Defeat and reprisal
steps.text: Tupac Katari was betrayed and executed in November 1781, and Diego Cristobal Tupac Amaru accepted a royal pardon at Sicuani in January 1782. The pardon did not last: in 1783 he and many relatives were executed on charges of renewed conspiracy. Spain banned Inca dress, titles and symbols, while abolishing the forced sales that had fuelled the revolt.

events.name: Execution of Tupac Katari
events.text: The Aymara leader was quartered near La Paz.

events.name: Peace of Sicuani
events.text: The last rebel leaders laid down their arms in exchange for a pardon.

name: Haitian Revolution
summary: Enslaved Africans in Saint-Domingue, France's richest colony, rose in 1791, won the abolition of slavery and, under Toussaint Louverture, drove out British and Spanish invaders. When Napoleon sent an army in 1802 to restore French rule and slavery, Jean-Jacques Dessalines led the resistance that, with yellow fever, destroyed it. Haiti declared independence in 1804 as the first nation founded by formerly enslaved people, a shock felt across the slaveholding Americas.

steps.label: Aug 1791
steps.title: The great uprising
steps.text: After a secret ceremony at Bois Caiman led by the vodou priest Dutty Boukman, tens of thousands of enslaved people on the Northern Plain rose in late August 1791. Within weeks they had burned over a thousand plantations and killed hundreds of planters, while the whites held out in Le Cap. Boukman was killed in November, but leaders such as Jean-Francois and Biassou kept the revolt alive.

events.name: Bois Caiman ceremony
events.text: A night gathering launched the coordinated revolt.

events.name: Burning of the Northern Plain
events.text: Rebels destroyed the plantations that made the colony rich.

steps.label: 1793 to 1794
steps.title: Abolition and invasion
steps.text: With France at war in Europe, Spain armed the rebels from Santo Domingo, and Toussaint rose to command under the Spanish flag. Britain invaded from Jamaica, taking Jeremie, Saint-Marc and Port-au-Prince. To win the Black population, commissioner Sonthonax abolished slavery in 1793, and when Paris confirmed abolition in 1794 Toussaint switched to the French Republic.

events.name: Abolition of slavery
events.text: Sonthonax freed the enslaved in the North; the Convention extended it to all French colonies in 1794.

events.name: British take Port-au-Prince
events.text: The colonial capital fell to a British expedition.

steps.label: 1795 to 1798
steps.title: Toussaint drives out the British
steps.text: Spain made peace in 1795 and ceded Santo Domingo to France. Toussaint, now a French general, built a disciplined army and pressed the British, who lost thousands of soldiers to yellow fever. In 1798 their commander Thomas Maitland negotiated a full withdrawal, handing over Port-au-Prince and the Mole Saint-Nicolas to Toussaint.

events.name: Santo Domingo ceded to France
events.text: By the Peace of Basel Spain gave its half of Hispaniola to France.

events.name: British evacuation
events.text: Maitland agreed to withdraw all British forces from the colony.

steps.label: 1799 to 1801
steps.title: Toussaint rules the island
steps.text: Toussaint defeated his rival André Rigaud, who held the South, in the bitter War of the Knives, in which Dessalines besieged Jacmel. In 1801 he marched into Spanish Santo Domingo and abolished slavery there, then issued a constitution making himself governor for life, still nominally under France.

events.name: Siege of Jacmel
events.text: Dessalines starved Rigaud's stronghold into surrender.

events.name: Occupation of Santo Domingo
events.text: Toussaint united all of Hispaniola under his command.

steps.title: Leclerc's expedition
steps.text: Napoleon sent his brother-in-law Charles Leclerc with some 30,000 troops to restore French control. Christophe burned Le Cap rather than surrender it, and the French paid heavily to take the fort of Crete-a-Pierrot, but Toussaint's generals began to yield. Toussaint surrendered, was seized by treachery and deported to France, where he died in 1803. When news came that France had restored slavery in Guadeloupe, the colony rose again, and yellow fever killed Leclerc and much of his army.

moves.label: French fleet lands at Le Cap

events.name: Burning of Le Cap
events.text: Christophe set the city ablaze as the French fleet arrived.

events.name: Battle of Crete-a-Pierrot
events.text: The French took the fort after weeks of costly assaults; its garrison broke out.

events.name: Arrest of Toussaint
events.text: Leclerc's men seized Toussaint near Ennery and shipped him to France.

steps.title: Vertieres
steps.text: Dessalines united Black and mixed-race commanders at Arcahaie under a new red and blue flag. The war became one of extermination on both sides as Rochambeau, Leclerc's successor, used terror, while renewed war with Britain cut French supply lines by sea. On 18 November Dessalines's army stormed the forts at Vertieres outside Le Cap, and Rochambeau surrendered and evacuated the colony.

fronts.label: Siege lines at Le Cap, Nov 1803

events.name: Congress of Arcahaie
events.text: Revolutionary leaders united under Dessalines and adopted a new flag.

events.name: Battle of Vertieres
events.text: The last French army in the colony was defeated and surrendered.

steps.label: 1 Jan 1804
steps.title: Independence
steps.text: At Gonaives on 1 January 1804 Dessalines declared the independence of Haiti, restoring the island's Taino name. In the following months most of the remaining French population was killed on his orders. The new state, the first born of a successful slave revolt, faced decades of isolation and a crippling indemnity demanded by France in 1825.

events.name: Declaration of independence
events.text: Haiti became the second independent nation in the Americas.

name: French Revolutionary Wars
summary: Revolutionary France went to war in 1792 against the monarchies of Europe, which feared the spread of the Revolution. Mass conscription and talented young generals turned near defeat into conquest of the Low Countries, the Rhineland and Italy, while Bonaparte's campaigns in Italy and Egypt made him famous and led him to power in 1799. The wars ended in the peace of Amiens in 1802, leaving France dominant on the continent and Britain at sea.

steps.title: Valmy and Jemappes
steps.text: France declared war on Austria in April 1792, and in summer a Prussian army under the Duke of Brunswick invaded, taking Longwy and Verdun on the road to Paris. At Valmy Kellermann and Dumouriez's citizen army stood firm under cannon fire and the Prussians turned back. Two days later France became a republic, and in November Dumouriez won at Jemappes and overran the Austrian Netherlands.

fronts.label: French line in the Argonne, Sept 1792

events.name: Battle of Valmy
events.text: A cannonade checked Brunswick's Prussians and saved the Revolution.

events.name: Battle of Jemappes
events.text: Dumouriez beat the Austrians and occupied Belgium.

steps.label: 1793 to 1794
steps.title: The nation in arms
steps.text: The king's execution brought Britain, Spain, the Dutch and others into a First Coalition, and France faced invasion on every frontier plus revolt at home. The Jacobin government decreed a levee en masse that raised over a million men. A young artillery officer, Bonaparte, helped retake Toulon from the British, and Jourdan's victory at Fleurus in 1794 reopened the road to Belgium and the Netherlands.

events.name: Siege of Toulon
events.text: Bonaparte's batteries forced the British fleet out of the great naval base.

events.name: Battle of Fleurus
events.text: Jourdan's victory, helped by a reconnaissance balloon, won Belgium for good.

steps.label: 1796 to 1797
steps.title: Bonaparte in Italy
steps.text: Prussia and Spain made peace in 1795 and Spain soon changed sides. In 1796 the 26 year old Bonaparte took over a ragged army at Nice, split the Piedmontese from the Austrians, took Milan and beat four Austrian armies sent to relieve Mantua, at Arcole and Rivoli among others. Advancing toward Vienna, he forced Austria to sign the Treaty of Campo Formio, giving France Belgium and a client republic in northern Italy.

events.name: Battle of Arcole
events.text: Bonaparte broke an Austrian relief army after three days in the marshes.

events.name: Battle of Rivoli
events.text: The decisive defeat of the last Austrian attempt to save Mantua.

events.name: Treaty of Campo Formio
events.text: Austria ceded Belgium and accepted French dominance in northern Italy.

steps.label: 1798 to 1801
steps.title: Expedition to Egypt
steps.text: To strike at Britain's route to India, Bonaparte sailed from Toulon with 35,000 men, took Malta and landed at Alexandria. He routed the Mamluks at the Pyramids, but Nelson destroyed his fleet at Aboukir Bay, stranding the army. An invasion of Syria failed before Acre, and Bonaparte slipped back to France in 1799; the army he left behind surrendered to the British and Ottomans in 1801.

moves.label: Up the Nile and into Syria

events.name: Battle of the Pyramids
events.text: French squares shattered the Mamluk cavalry and opened Cairo.

events.name: Battle of the Nile
events.text: Nelson destroyed the French fleet at anchor in Aboukir Bay.

events.name: Siege of Acre
events.text: Ottoman defenders and British sailors held the city and ended the Syrian campaign.

steps.title: The Second Coalition
steps.text: Austria, Russia, Britain and the Ottomans joined a new coalition. Archduke Charles pushed the French back across the Rhine, while Suvorov's Russians and Austrians swept them out of Italy, winning at the Trebbia and Novi. Masséna saved France at the Second Battle of Zurich, and Suvorov fought his way out over the Alps. In November Bonaparte, back from Egypt, seized power as First Consul.

moves.label: Russians through Italy and over the Alps

events.name: Battle of Novi
events.text: Suvorov's victory completed the Allied reconquest of northern Italy.

events.name: Second Battle of Zurich
events.text: Massena crushed Korsakov's Russians before Suvorov could join them.

events.name: Coup of 18 Brumaire
events.text: Bonaparte overthrew the Directory and became First Consul.

steps.title: Marengo and Hohenlinden
steps.text: Bonaparte led a reserve army over the snowbound Great St Bernard Pass into the Austrians' rear in Italy. At Marengo he was all but beaten until Desaix's division arrived and turned the battle, and the Austrians gave up northern Italy. In December Moreau destroyed the main Austrian army at Hohenlinden, east of Munich, opening the road to Vienna.

events.name: Battle of Marengo
events.text: A late counter-attack turned defeat into victory and secured Bonaparte's rule.

events.name: Battle of Hohenlinden
events.text: Moreau's crushing victory forced Austria to seek peace.

steps.label: 1801 to 1802
steps.title: Peace of Luneville and Amiens
steps.text: Austria accepted the Rhine frontier and French control of northern Italy at Luneville in February 1801. A British army landed in Egypt, beat the French at Alexandria and forced the last French troops there to surrender, while Nelson broke the Danish fleet at Copenhagen. Exhausted, Britain and France signed the Treaty of Amiens in March 1802, a peace that lasted barely a year.

events.name: Treaty of Luneville
events.text: Austria left the war, ending the Second Coalition on the continent.

events.name: Battle of Alexandria
events.text: Abercromby's victory led to the French surrender in Egypt.

events.name: Treaty of Amiens
events.text: Britain and France made peace, ending ten years of war.

name: Napoleonic Wars
summary: Napoleon's French Empire and its satellites fought a series of coalitions financed by Britain and fielded mainly by Austria, Russia and Prussia. Napoleon dominated the continent after Austerlitz, Jena and Friedland, but the Peninsular War and the disaster in Russia in 1812 broke his power, and he was defeated at Leipzig, forced to abdicate in 1814 and finally beaten at Waterloo in 1815. The wars spread French law and administration, awakened nationalism and left Britain the leading world power after the Congress of Vienna.

steps.title: War of the Third Coalition
steps.text: Britain had been at war with France again since 1803, and Napoleon, crowned emperor in 1804, gathered an invasion army at Boulogne. When Austria and Russia joined Britain he marched the Grande Armee to the Danube, trapped Mack's Austrians at Ulm and took Vienna, while Nelson destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet at Trafalgar. At Austerlitz Napoleon routed the Russian and Austrian armies, and Austria made peace at Pressburg.

moves.label: Russian army falls back to Olmutz

events.name: Ulm
events.text: Napoleon encircled Mack's army, which surrendered with about 25,000 men.

events.name: Battle of Trafalgar
events.text: Nelson destroyed the Franco-Spanish fleet and died in the battle, ending any French hope of invading Britain.

events.name: Battle of Austerlitz
events.text: Napoleon broke the allied centre on the Pratzen Heights in his most celebrated victory.

steps.label: 1806 to 1807
steps.title: War of the Fourth Coalition
steps.text: Napoleon replaced the Holy Roman Empire with his Confederation of the Rhine, and Prussia went to war. In one day at Jena and Auerstedt the Prussian army was destroyed and Napoleon entered Berlin, then pushed into Poland against the Russians. After a bloody draw at Eylau he won at Friedland, and the Treaties of Tilsit made Tsar Alexander his ally.

moves.label: Through Thuringia to Berlin and Poland

events.name: Battle of Jena-Auerstedt
events.text: Twin French victories destroyed the Prussian army in a single day.

events.name: Battle of Friedland
events.text: Napoleon routed Bennigsen's Russians and forced the Tsar to seek peace.

events.name: Treaties of Tilsit
events.text: Russia became France's ally and Prussia lost half its territory.

steps.title: The Peninsular War begins
steps.text: Napoleon occupied Portugal, then deposed the Spanish Bourbons and made his brother Joseph king of Spain, setting off a national uprising. A Spanish army forced a French corps to surrender at Bailen and Wellesley's British army freed Portugal, so Napoleon came in person, retook Madrid and chased Sir John Moore's army to Corunna. The war in Iberia became a running sore that drained French strength for six years.

fronts.label: French fall back to the Ebro, Aug 1808

moves.label: Moore's advance and retreat to Corunna

events.name: Battle of Bailen
events.text: Castanos forced Dupont's corps to surrender, the first defeat of a Napoleonic army in the field.

events.name: Napoleon enters Madrid
events.text: Napoleon smashed the Spanish armies and reinstalled Joseph in the capital.

events.name: Battle of Corunna
events.text: Moore held off Soult so his army could escape by sea, but was killed.

steps.title: War of the Fifth Coalition
steps.text: With Napoleon's best troops in Spain, Austria struck again. Napoleon beat Archduke Charles in Bavaria and took Vienna, but his attempt to cross the Danube was thrown back at Aspern-Essling, his first personal defeat. Six weeks later he crossed in force and won the huge battle of Wagram, and Austria made peace and gave Napoleon an archduchess as wife, while Wellesley won at Talavera in Spain.

moves.label: Austrian invasion of Bavaria and retreat to the Marchfeld
Napoleon to Vienna and across the Danube

events.name: Battle of Aspern-Essling
events.text: Archduke Charles threw Napoleon back across the Danube.

events.name: Battle of Wagram
events.text: Napoleon won a two-day battle of over 300,000 men and forced Austria to make peace.

events.name: Battle of Talavera
events.text: Wellesley repulsed the French and was made Viscount Wellington.

steps.label: 1810 to 1812
steps.title: Invasion of Russia
steps.text: In Iberia Wellington held Massena at the Lines of Torres Vedras in 1810 and won at Salamanca in 1812. Meanwhile Russia broke with the Continental System, and Napoleon crossed the Niemen with over 600,000 men. The Russians retreated, fought at Borodino and abandoned Moscow, which burned; when the Tsar would not negotiate, the Grande Armee retreated through the winter and was almost destroyed.

events.name: Battle of Salamanca
events.text: Wellington routed Marmont's army in a swift flank attack.

events.name: Battle of Borodino
events.text: The bloodiest day of the wars left Napoleon the field and the road to Moscow, but not a decisive victory.

events.name: Crossing of the Berezina
events.text: Napoleon escaped across the river on improvised bridges but lost tens of thousands.

steps.title: War of the Sixth Coalition
steps.text: Prussia and then Austria and Sweden joined Russia and Britain. Napoleon rebuilt an army and won at Lutzen, Bautzen and Dresden, but three allied armies closed on him at Leipzig, where the Battle of the Nations drove him out of Germany. In Spain Wellington broke Joseph's army at Vitoria and pushed the French back to the Pyrenees.

events.name: Battle of Vitoria
events.text: Wellington broke Joseph Bonaparte's army and ended French rule in Spain.

events.name: Battle of Dresden
events.text: Napoleon's last great victory in Germany drove back the Army of Bohemia.

events.name: Battle of Leipzig
events.text: The Battle of the Nations, the largest battle in Europe before 1914, drove Napoleon out of Germany.

steps.title: The fall of Paris
steps.text: The allies invaded France from the east while Wellington crossed the Pyrenees in the south. Napoleon won a string of brilliant victories in the Six Days' Campaign but could not stop the converging armies, and Paris fell on 31 March. His marshals refused to fight on, and he abdicated at Fontainebleau and was exiled to Elba as the Bourbons returned.

moves.label: Army of Silesia across the Rhine
Napoleon strikes between the allied armies

events.name: Six Days' Campaign
events.text: Napoleon beat Blucher's scattered corps at Champaubert, Montmirail and Vauchamps.

events.name: Battle of Paris
events.text: The allies stormed the heights around Paris and the city capitulated.

events.name: Abdication at Fontainebleau
events.text: Napoleon gave up his throne and was sent to Elba.

steps.label: Mar to Jun 1815
steps.title: The Hundred Days and Waterloo
steps.text: Napoleon escaped from Elba and marched on Paris as the army rallied to him, while Murat in Naples rose in his support and was crushed. He struck into Belgium and beat the Prussians at Ligny, but at Waterloo Wellington's army held until Blucher arrived, and the French army collapsed. Napoleon was exiled to Saint Helena and the Congress of Vienna redrew the map of Europe.

polities: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.name: Battle of Ligny
events.text: Napoleon defeated Blucher, but the Prussian army withdrew intact.

events.name: Battle of Waterloo
events.text: Wellington's army held until the Prussians arrived, and Napoleon's army broke.

events.name: Congress of Vienna
events.text: The victors restored monarchies and set a balance of power that lasted decades.

name: Serbian Revolution and Greek War of Independence
summary: Between 1804 and 1830 Serbs and then Greeks rose against Ottoman rule in the first national revolutions of the Balkans. Serbia won autonomy after two uprisings, and the Greek revolt, near defeat after Egypt intervened, was saved when Britain, France and Russia destroyed the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at Navarino and Russia beat the Ottomans in 1828 to 1829. Autonomous Serbia and an independent Greece began the long break-up of Ottoman Europe.

steps.label: 1804 to 1806
steps.title: The First Serbian Uprising
steps.text: In the Pashalik of Belgrade, renegade janissaries murdered Serbian notables, and in 1804 the Serbs rose under the livestock trader Karadjordje. A revolt against local tyrants became a war against the Sultan: the rebels beat Ottoman armies at Ivankovac and Misar and took Belgrade. When Russia went to war with the Ottomans in 1806 it backed the Serbs.

events.name: Orasac assembly
events.text: Serbian leaders chose Karadjordje to lead the uprising.

events.name: Battle of Ivankovac
events.text: The first rebel victory over a regular Ottoman army turned the revolt into a war with the Sultan.

events.name: Battle of Misar
events.text: Karadjordje defeated the Bosnian army, and Belgrade fell to the rebels that winter.

steps.label: 1809 to 1817
steps.title: Defeat and the Second Uprising
steps.text: Napoleon's invasion pulled Russia out of the war in 1812, and in 1813 Ottoman armies converged on Serbia from three sides, retook Belgrade and drove Karadjordje into exile. In 1815 Milos Obrenovic raised a second uprising at Takovo and won a negotiated autonomy, becoming prince of Serbia. Karadjordje returned in 1817 and was murdered on Milos's orders.

events.name: Battle of Cegar
events.text: Stevan Sindjelic blew up his own redoubt; the Ottomans built the Skull Tower from the dead.

events.name: Fall of Belgrade
events.text: The Ottoman reconquest ended the first uprising and Karadjordje fled to Austria.

events.name: Takovo uprising
events.text: Milos Obrenovic launched the second revolt, which won Serbian autonomy.

steps.label: 1821 to 1822
steps.title: The Greek Revolution
steps.text: The secret Filiki Eteria launched the revolt: Ypsilantis crossed into Moldavia but was crushed at Dragasani, while the Peloponnese rose in March 1821. Kolokotronis took Tripolitsa, the Greek fleet ruled the Aegean, and Dramali Pasha's great army was destroyed in the passes at Dervenakia. The Ottomans massacred the islanders of Chios, a crime that turned European opinion toward the Greeks.

moves.label: Sacred Band in the Danubian Principalities

events.name: Siege of Tripolitsa
events.text: Kolokotronis stormed the Ottoman capital of the Morea, followed by a massacre of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants.

events.name: Chios massacre
events.text: Ottoman troops killed or enslaved most of the island's Greek population.

events.name: Battle of Dervenakia
events.text: Kolokotronis trapped and destroyed Dramali's army in the mountain passes.
